dag.description: Bedrock LLM weak-supervision labeling feeding a PyTorch classifier with percentile (rank) score calibration. Pre-staged (Dummy-loaded) data is preprocessed, enriched/scored by Bedrock under a generated prompt template, then labeled by a generated label ruleset before PyTorch training. A mirrored calibration branch threads through Bedrock + label-ruleset execution, is scored by PyTorchModelEval, calibrated with PercentileModelCalibration, then packaged and registered.

cost.estimated_hours: 4-14 (Bedrock labeling on both branches + GPU PyTorch training)

agent_context.when_to_use: You need LLM-derived (weak-supervision) labels via Bedrock plus a declarative label ruleset to train a PyTorch classifier, AND you want percentile/rank-based score calibration for percentile-threshold enforcement rather than probability calibration. This is the rnr_pytorch_bedrock EU training DAG: Bedrock scores/enriches pre-staged data under a generated prompt template, a generated label ruleset derives labels, PyTorch trains, and PercentileModelCalibration produces rank-bucketed scores for the enforcement threshold.
agent_context.when_not_to_use: If you need standard probability calibration, use bedrock_pytorch_with_label_ruleset_e2e (ModelCalibration). If you already have ground-truth labels, drop the Bedrock+LabelRuleset front-end and use pytorch_percentile_e2e. If you do not need any LLM labeling, use a plain PyTorch or XGBoost DAG. If data is Cradle-sourced and you only want to emit labels (no training), use bedrock_cradle_label_ruleset_labeling.
differentiators: LLM weak-supervision: Bedrock (prompt-template-gated) + LabelRulesetGeneration/Execution derive the training labels
Percentile (rank) calibration instead of probability calibration — for percentile-threshold enforcement
Both training and calibration branches are threaded through Bedrock + label-ruleset execution
16 nodes / 19 edges — the percentile-calibrated sibling of bedrock_pytorch_with_label_ruleset_e2e

prerequisites.how: BedrockPromptTemplateGeneration produces the template consumed by both BedrockProcessing steps
LabelRulesetGeneration emits the ruleset applied by both LabelRulesetExecution steps

common_pitfalls: Prompt template and label ruleset must be identical/consistent across the training and calibration branches
Package consumes PyTorchTraining output (the model), not PercentileModelCalibration output
LabelRulesetExecution depends on BOTH BedrockProcessing output and the generated ruleset
